brief.headline: Push for a 10–15% price cut: they keep 5.9% profit vs 3.8% peer average, so there's room.

priceAsk.summary: Ask for a 10–15% price reduction on rigid plastic packaging.
priceAsk.target: Target ₹0.65–0.80/pc for 28 mm caps (current market asking ₹0.85–0.95/pc typical)
priceAsk.basis: They keep 5.9% of every ₹100 they sell, well above the 3.8% that similar firms keep — that extra margin is room for us. Market asking price for 28 mm induction-wad PP caps shows modest headroom to ₹0.65–0.80 at higher volume.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Offer to pay 15 days earlier (15 days instead of 30) in exchange for a price cut worth roughly their 12.19% borrowing rate — about 0.5% off the price.
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: Paying 15 days earlier frees up ₹22.57 L cash for us, but costs them that same cash earlier — which is worth their borrowing rate (12.19%) to them, so trade it for a cut.

brief.financialLeverage: Chemco is healthy — CRISIL A+ / Stable rating, makes ₹937.60 Cr revenue, keeps 5.9% profit. But their cash is stuck for 104d vs 79d at similar firms, so cash is tighter than peers. We're ₹5.49 Cr or 0.59% of their sales — small, but they're growing fast (22.1%/yr) and want volume. Push hard on price (they have margin headroom), but also dangle faster payment or more volume to close the gap.

evidence.point: They keep 5.9% profit, well above the 3.8% peer median — extra margin we can tap.
Their cash is stuck for 104d vs 79d at similar firms, so they value faster payment.
They already pay their own suppliers slower than peers — 49d vs 37d — so asking them to give us more time is only fair.
They borrow money at about 12.19%, so paying them 15 days early is worth roughly 0.5% of the price to them.
Market asking price for 28 mm PP caps is ₹0.85–0.95/pc typical, with headroom to ₹0.65–0.80 at higher volume.
We spend ₹5.49 Cr with them, only 0.59% of their ₹937.60 Cr revenue — but they're growing 22.1%/yr and want orders.

alternates.name: Manjushree Technopack Ltd
alternates.why: India's largest rigid-plastic packaging converter — pharma bottles, caps, preforms; ₹2569.83 Cr revenue, health score B (65/100). Top second-source candidate.

alternates.name: Mold-Tek Packaging Ltd
alternates.why: Listed rigid-plastic leader (pails, containers, pharma); strong, profitable — a robust alternate for bottles and closures.

alternates.name: Pearl Polymers Ltd
alternates.why: Listed PET bottle/jar specialist (Pearlpet) — direct fit for PET bottles.

risks: We're only 0.59% of their sales — a small customer — so our volume threat is limited unless we can credibly bundle more business or show a qualified second source.
They sit in the grey zone (Altman Z 2.17) — not distressed, but not rock-solid either. Don't squeeze so hard they stumble; keep the relationship stable while you line up a backup.
Their cash is stuck longer than peers (104d vs 79d), so if you push payment terms out further without a price give, they may push back hard or ask for a deposit.

Market asking price for caps shows only 'modest headroom' to ₹0.65–0.80 at higher volume — so a 15% cut may need a volume commitment or looser spec; prepare to justify the ask with a credible volume increase or second-source plan.
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: You've been a solid partner, but we see room to close the gap — your margin runs 5.9% vs 3.8% at similar firms, and the market line for caps shows headroom, so let's talk about a 10–15% price cut and how we structure payment and volume to make it work for both of us.
